It’s different every single time you open the app. Amazon requires DAILY verification to load in transactions, what a joke. This app is hardly worth paying for lol. The team takes feedback and implements recommended improvements. Try it out!
The best budgeting app out there!. The app is great and the team is responsive and constantly improving the experience. I 10/10 recommend!

Don’t expect a functional app. For over a year now my wife and I have been more or less completely unable to use Copilot due to ridiculous performance issues across every surface it’s available. Best Budgeting App. Love this app. The bank integration alone saves me so much time—I can actually see all my spending without manually tracking everything. UI looks great and feels easy to navigate. The support team is super responsive too, which is nice when you have feature ideas. My only wish is more chart options, but it's already doing exactly what I need. I get immense value out of this app and have been a user for a few years now with no plans to go elsewhere.

Great Budgeting App & View Multiple Accounts at Once. My wife and I have been using this app for over half a year now and I love that we can easily review all of our bank accounts, investments, and loans all in one place.  I previously managed all of this on my own before we found this solution and it’s so much better than having to share access or get her signed up to view all of the various accounts separately.  We use it for household budgets and retirement and vacation planning goals as well.  My only complaint is that you need to reverify your Amazon account almost daily.  We have a lot of purchases that come from there and if you want them to be properly sorted into the correct budget category you need to assign them when the come in.  That’s easy once they have been synced with Amazon, but it’s very annoying to have to sign in again and again so often.  Copilot is able to sync with very secure financial institutions, from our 401ks to our mortgage accounts, so it’s very surprising that there isn’t a more straightforward way to at least save the login information into the app of desktop portal to more easily sync itemized purchased made there.  It would easily be a 5-star experience if they could ever make that happen.

From 5 to 3 stars. I love the interface because it’s colorful and easy to navigate. It’s so easy to categorize transactions and see where all of your money is. The rollover feature is perfect for me rather than having to track individual sinking funds. It didn’t take long to set up at all, and it shows me everything I need without having to run reports or search for it, such as the average amount I’m spending per category per month, which updates automatically. I’m switching from YNAB, and I hated the give every dollar a job model. In Copilot Money, you don’t have to move assigned dollars between categories every time money moves between your accounts. This app has given me the flexibility I need in my budget while still maintaining control over my finances. My one suggestion is to add an auto-distribute function for splitting transactions so I don’t have to manually calculate sales tax for each category.

EDIT: I have canceled my free trial and will be going back to spreadsheets. So far the customer support has been good. One of my accounts will not connect and they have been working diligently to resolve the issue - much appreciated. However, I discovered that a bunch of my transactions are missing. Initially, when I connected my accounts, it imported 2 1/2 years worth of data. I had to manually delete everything prior to this year, which was difficult because I kept trying to delete things and they wouldn’t disappear so I had to do it repeatedly. Now I’m discovering that most of my categories are missing transactions between January and April 2026. I tried entering them manually but it’s a bit tedious. I can’t customize the color of the accounts and when I search for them, the font is too small so it’s difficult to find the one I’m looking for plus they always come up in a different order. I also don’t like that I cannot re-order my categories or my recurrings. Speaking of recurrings, the app is not recognizing new transactions, even though I have set up a rule for the name. Some of my recurrings are duplicated and I can’t rename them. Visually the list is a mess. In addition, I have to agree with other users that there is no easy way to see what is available to spend. I find myself toggling back-and-forth between the cash flow tab, the dashboard and my categories but still not feeling certain about the information it’s giving me. Yesterday I was reviewing new transactions and one of them was categorized incorrectly even though I have at least five other transactions from the same place. When I re-categorized it, I found that all the previous transactions were also categorized incorrectly, even though I’ve already gone through every single transaction in my history and made sure that it was right. Somehow it got changed? I really like the layout of this app and at first it seemed great but now I’m finding too many functional errors.

Unfortunately, if you do not have one of the major five banks, you will probably have issues. Amazing. Absolutely! Here's something that feels warm, enthusiastic, and conversational—very much in your style.

I've tried more budgeting and finance apps than I care to admit, and **Copilot Money** is hands down the best I've ever used.

What really sets it apart is how incredibly easy it is to use. Within minutes I had a clear picture of where my money was going. The visual dashboards are beautiful, intuitive, and actually make you *want* to check your finances. The analytics are next-level, giving insights that are both meaningful and actionable without feeling overwhelming.

So Close To Being Really Good. I really wanted to use Copilot and tried to make it work, but there were too many little annoyances that finally made me give up. 

One of them was having to manually create two transactions for things like my car payment. For whatever reason, Plaid couldn’t connect to my car loan account, so I had to manually add it. The rigamarole of having to create manual transactions to debit the money from my checking and the create another transaction to my car loan account to show the payment was time consuming, frustrating, and quite frankly unnecessary. Being able to transfer money from a payment account to a loan account should be one transaction.  I had three loan accounts I would have to do this for. 

I also found the iPad version of Copilot slow, sometimes unresponsive, unintuitive, and quite inferior to the iPhone app.  Things in the iPad app did not work the same and were missing features. For example, when entering a manual internal transfer, the “incoming” or “outgoing” selector buttons were not available. Sometimes clicking on a field would bring up a numeric keypad while other times in would bring up a full keyboard. 

Finally, Copilot relies heavily on Plaid for connecting to banks. Unfortunately, this system was much less reliable than what I found in other finance apps. 

I would be willing to give Copilot another shot once they are able to update the iPad app and fix a lot of these issues.

I have to export ALL my transactions, dating back to when I first started using the app, to a spreadsheet, then filter my searches there. This is particularly vexing at tax time. 

Other, less-pressing problems (for me) have to do with look-and-feel issues, and so are completely subjective.

Navigating to text fields within the app has never felt intuitive. 

Year-end summary does not allow me to page to whichever category I want to see - I can only move forward-back one page at a time in the order Copilot has arranged for me. If you’re going to include a “feature,” fine, but design it in a way that anticipates users wanting to do more with it than just passively follow the directions onscreen.

There was an issue with my PayPal account needing to be re-synced daily. This seems to have been fixed recently, but other accounts also lose sync occasionally.

Again, for the price, this app is a solid choice for tracking and organizing finances. But it could be so much more if the designers made up their minds to do a better job of meeting the needs and expectations of their users.

Beautiful app, but progress on missing features is slow. This is a gorgeous, Apple-native finance app that’s full of clever features and design decisions. I like so much of it that I want to use it for my bookkeeping, but a number of issues prevent that. First, it’s wild that you cannot see or edit any rules you make for categorizing your expenses. I know you can contact support and they’ll delete a rule for you, but the fact that this has remained an issue for years makes me question priorities. 

I need a way of marking charges as shared/split (and specifically, rules to do this automatically…), which ultimately makes it impossible for me to actually track my budget with this app. I know this isn’t the most common scenario, but it’s also not rare. 

The prioritization of things like Genmoji integration (cute!) or most recently a web app (useful!) to me feel less important than filling some of the missing features that actually let you control your budget. And the team is small enough that there’s maybe one major feature a year. That pace is fine once the foundation is there, but it feels like the app has a lot of low hanging fruit that may take years to get to. 

Again, I want to use this app — it’s so much nicer than a homegrown Google Sheet or any of the other big apps! But if it doesn’t currently fully match your needs, it probably won’t for a long time.

Excellent, life changing. But, needs refinement. Copilot is an excellent app that more than deserves 5 stars. I’ve been using the app since 2021, and have gotten 8 people to start using it. As a longtime user, I do have several feature requests that I believe could improve and refine this great app. Some of these are cosmetic and others are seriously annoying things that they really should fix.

1. Please please fix graphs. When you have a category that you used to spend a lot in but now spend a lot less, the bars are barely visible. The bars should scale according to the local max on the screen and not the global max which is potentially from years ago. This can render the graph completely useless. The graphs in investing and accounts also need a refresh. I don’t find them useful as they are too small! Give us better graphs and just data visualization in general. 
2. Rules absolutely NEED a redesign like yesterday. The fact you can’t manage your rules at this point is insane. Second, please let us create a rule without needing to apply it to every transaction it finds ever. I have years of specific categorization that I don’t necessarily want to mass change just to set a rule. Just let us set a rule for future transactions only. This makes no sense 
3. We should be able to archive a category or hide it from view somehow but keep the totals in your numbers. I used to vape and I don’t need a vapes category anymore but also don’t want to just delete all the spending or put it into miscellaneous. 
4. I would love to be able to group groups. For example I have my car group and also another transportation group that has public and ride share. I’d love to be able to group these 2 so I can know how much I’m spending on transportation total, but also be able to drill down into how much I spend on my car. Adding Ubers to my car group would not let me see just how much I spend on my car but also I have to sum 2 groups to know my transportation spend.
Anyway keep killing it copilot team. I’ve seen yall release some bangers so I have faith this app will only get better. Also please don’t forget us users with a ton of data, I have been through periods where performance has suffered very badly but yall have fixed it so please don’t stop addressing that.

Terrible link to plaid. The CoPilot app itself is solid. The interface is intuitive, the budgeting tools are thoughtfully designed, and the categorization engine is one of the few that actually learns user behavior instead of making a mess after every single transaction. If I were rating only CoPilot’s internal functionality, it would easily be a five-star product. The problem is everything that sits between CoPilot and the banks it needs to talk to.

Navy Federal and the Plaid integration are, frankly, hot garbage. Nothing connects correctly, nothing stays synced, and the error messages are so vague that you end up wasting time troubleshooting problems the app can’t fix because the underlying data link simply doesn’t work. Every attempt to authenticate with Navy Federal through Plaid turns into a full-scale exercise in frustration, circular prompts, and outright failure. When the main value of a budgeting app depends on accurate account aggregation, having your primary financial institution break the entire workflow is unacceptable.

What makes this even more frustrating is that CoPilot could be outstanding—its design is genuinely strong. But none of that matters if the connectivity layer collapses every single time. When your bank accounts won’t stay linked and half the transactions never load, you’re left with an expensive app that functions worse than a notebook. At this point, using graph paper would be more reliable than dealing with this dysfunctional chain of broken connections.

CoPilot deserves credit for what it controls, but Navy Fed and Plaid drag the experience down so far that the usefulness of the app is severely compromised. Until those two decide to operate at even a minimally functional level, CoPilot’s potential is wasted.
